thread:
amy (AMY Sales): quick sync — ACME POC asks: private deployment with no public internet egress, wants recommendation PrivateLink vs VPC peering, firewall rule list, TLS-inspection impacts, and a POC cost ballpark. POC scope: 2 weeks, ~5k req/day, ~50GB/day. @lina @devon @sanjay

lina (Solutions Eng): short take: both options workable. PrivateLink (interface endpoints) = simpler from customer firewall perspective (only outbound to ENIs, SG controls). VPC Peering = full L3, more flexible but needs route discipline and can leak routes if not careful. Key trade: PrivateLink => we expose ENIs they must allow. Peering => endpoints preserve original source IPs more easily.

devon (Network Eng): quick network notes: if customer needs source-IP preservation for downstream logging, VPC Peering + a NAT/proxy in their VPC is easiest. PrivateLink terminates at our ENIs so the customer will see our ENI IPs as source (they must allow those). We can list the ENI CIDRs per-region/account for the POC. Also consider cross-account route tables for peering.

sanjay (Security): on TLS inspection: if the customer's security team wants to perform TLS MITM (decrypt & inspect), they must place the TLS-inspecting proxy in front of the path to our endpoints (i.e., in their egress path). Redwood will not intercept customer-decrypted traffic. We do support mTLS and client cert enrollment for Private deployments. Also need to confirm compliance level (PCI/ISO/HIPAA) — that affects whether they can inspect or require end-to-end TLS.

amy (AMY Sales): pricing asks: they want to know if PrivateLink adds infra egress costs and whether Redwood charges extra. they said 50GB/day for POC. can we give a quick estimate?

lina (Solutions Eng): pricing note: typical breakdown — (1) cloud infra costs paid by customer (interface endpoint per-hour + data processed charges in AWS/GCP), (2) Redwood private deployment fee (platform + support). For a two-week POC we can cover infra cost via credits if needed — need sales-ops approval. I'll put together a POC pricing one-pager. :memo:

devon (Network Eng): firewall snippet customers usually ask for (example):

```
# Customer outbound firewall (example)
# Allow outbound to Redwood PrivateLink ENIs (customer initiates)
ALLOW TCP 443 to 10.200.128.0/26    # example ENI CIDR (we'll supply final)
# If using VPC Peering and our public egress (NAT) paths (only for hybrid)
ALLOW TCP 443 to 52.33.44.0/24     # example Redwood egress NAT pool (if used)
# If they route via corporate proxy
ALLOW TCP 3128 to proxy.internal.corp (proxy IPs)
# DNS
ALLOW UDP 53 to 10.0.0.2 (customer DNS resolver)
```

devon (Network Eng): note: if customer has TLS-inspect appliances that break SNI, we recommend they preserve SNI for host-based routing. If they cannot, then we need an L7 proxy in their environment to route to the correct service.

sanjay (Security): security questionnaire checklist for us to provide: 
- SOC2 report (latest)
- Data flow diagram (POC-specific)
- KMS/HSM integration notes (we support customer-managed KMS for Private)
- TLS/mTLS options and cert rotation policy
- Pen test summary + contact for vulnerability disclosures
I'll assemble and upload to the shared folder.

amy (AMY Sales): customer follow-ups I'm going to ask them: 1) do they prefer PrivateLink or Peering? 2) will they perform TLS inspect? 3) do they require source-IP to be preserved for logging? 4) fill security questionnaire draft (I'll send).

lina (Solutions Eng): action items: I'll draft a simple network diagram for both flows (PrivateLink vs Peering) and a one-page POC pricing sheet. devon will add ENI CIDR ranges and firewall snippet we can give to customer.

devon (Network Eng): will do — I'll also attach a minimal terraform snippet for PrivateLink consumer setup if they want IaC. snippet (example):

```
resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "redwood_private" {
  vpc_id            = var.customer_vpc_id
  service_name      = "com.redwood.inference.private"
  vpc_endpoint_type = "Interface"
  subnet_ids        = var.subnet_ids
  security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.allow_redwood.id]
}
```

sanjay (Security): timeline: if they return the questionnaire today we can turn security bundle within 3 business days. For KMS/HSM integration we need their KMS ARN and key policy during onboarding.

amy (AMY Sales): final blocker for the deal: they want assurance that POC won't incur unexpected network egress charges. lina — include a clear network-cost note and a contact at sales-ops to request infra credits if needed. I'll confirm SLA for the POC (uptime expectation). :thumbsup:
